text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swedish forestry group Stora AB on Wednesday said its 1996 profit after financial items plunged 71 percent to 2.3 billion crowns from a record profit of more than eight billion in 1995. Stora was the first of Swedish forestry groups to release 1996 earnings and its result is a bad omen for the sector.

- Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink does not share the EMU views of Education Minister Carl Tham, he told the newspaper. In a Wednesday column in the newspaper Carl Tham painted a negative picture of Europe's planned Economic and Monetary Union. "A lot is positive with EMU, but there are also disadvantages," Asbrink said.
- A weak crown has been an important reason for the Riksbank, the central bank, not to cut its key repo rate this year, deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten said at a seminar on Wednesday.

- Swedish prices are rising so inflation will pick up again, the newspaper concluded after studying price increases in several areas, for example higher rents and higher prices on cigarettes, alcohol, drugs and petrol.

- Adjustments to both a common European currency and a new century are hardly possible to deal with at the same time, neither for the public administration nor for the private industry, according to a report by an IT committee set up by Communications Minister Ines Uusmann. The report is due to be published shortly.

- Lars Leijonborg is expected to accept the job as leader for the Liberal Party on Thursday. He would replace Maria Leissner who stepped down recently on the grounds she did not feel she had enough support within the party. Leijonborg has acted as party leader in parliament as Leissner does not have a parliamentary seat.

- Axel Johnson AB, a family-owned trading company with sales of 30 billion crowns and a workforce of 15,000, may list one or more of its retail or foods companies. Company president Goran Ennerfelt says there is a possibility some firm could be listed on the Stockholm bourse this year although there are no immediate, concrete plans. The group is divided into three firms with the largest part of the group Axel Johnson AB, which includes foods wholesaler Dagab, grocery store chain Hemkop, Saba Trading and the Pressbyran chain.

- Swedish newspaper Dagens Nyheter, owned by the Marieberg publishing group, plans to invest 100 million crowns to establish the country's leading Internet operation. The newspaper's target is to break even within three years.

- The Swedish government now expects that GDP will increase faster in 1997 than the 2.3 percent increase predicted in the autumn. Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said a revised GDP forecast will be presented by the finance ministry on April 15.

- Forestry group Stora AB reported its pre-tax profit for 1996 fell by 71 percent due to lower product prices. Pre-tax profit fell to 2.3 billion crowns from eight billion in 1995 which was below average analyst forecasts for a pre-tax profit of 2.5 billion crowns.
